dossiers.title: Moon Hunters
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 10 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: Brief action-RPG dungeon fighting combines with choices and repeated heroes' lives; the central appeal is seeing how encounters alter a character's mythology.
Each roughly five-day adventure is short, and new characters, classes, choices and endings encourage successive runs rather than a single long linear campaign.
Players report very quick repeat playthroughs and complain that the map encounters and combat are not deep enough to sustain much repetition.
Russian and English-language players highlight social or family play as especially enjoyable and sometimes more engaging than single-player.
Early Russian discussions include reports of difficulty with gamepad assignment and local multiplayer connections; these are historical version-specific reports.
The mythology, character illustration and soundtrack earn praise, while some players find the world areas visually basic compared with detailed character images.
Replays reveal different legends and paths, yet some players say the choices and true-ending unlock rules are too obscure or have disappointingly limited effects.
Players who want tactical action criticize repetitive enemies and basic button-driven combat, notwithstanding the inventive story concept.
Its compact format makes it feasible to finish a run in one sitting but leaves some players wishing for more story development and substantive new quests.
A December 2025 review credits the developers with implementing LAN connections after prior online server shutdown, but this does not verify every present multiplayer configuration.

conflicts.statement: One player treasures the co-op memories while another thinks the story and encounters are underdeveloped despite the inventive premise.

dossiers.title: Absolute Drift
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 10 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: Top-down drifting rewards controlled slides, sustained combos, clipping corner markers and avoiding walls rather than overtaking AI vehicles.
The handling initially punishes imprecise steering and speed but can feel gratifying once a player learns to maintain drift angles.
Several free-roam districts link score challenges, drift tracks and mountain runs, with the possibility of selecting specialized events.
Meeting score and trick objectives opens more zones and cars, with optional records and leaderboards extending mastery.
The main game remains drifting rather than racing opponents; novelty comes from new curves, vehicles and ambitious combo targets.
Players praise clean minimal graphics and an electronic soundtrack for supporting concentration on movement.
The gap between basic completion and high scoring or fully completing challenges is steep.
Short sessions of free driving are possible, while chasing flawless challenge records takes repeated careful attempts.
The experience has leaderboard and ghost comparisons, while players explicitly note the absence of normal head-to-head multiplayer racing.
Car handling differences, steering sensitivity and manual control options reward experimentation rather than instant arcade driving.

conflicts.statement: Players describe simple short-session goals but demanding high-skill drift performance, so initial accessibility and long-term difficulty should be distinguished.

dossiers.title: Grow Home
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 11 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: A small robot climbs by independently gripping with two hands while encouraging a giant plant to grow branch by branch up toward a hovering ship.
Independent left and right grips make climbing initially awkward and physics-based, but this unusual tactile control is the core of the platforming.
Collectible crystals and new tools, including floating leaves and a jetpack, allow increasingly elaborate routes and high-altitude movement.
Floating islands, animals, strange flora and optional hidden collectibles invite vertical exploration while players choose where to send plant shoots.
It is a compact journey often completed in several hours, offering relaxation and exploration without a sprawling plot or combat campaign.
The cheerful small robot and low-poly alien world carry the tone, and one recent player found the same charm that they remembered from earlier years.
Falls and bad grips can be frustrating, but the overall platforming avoids intense combat and often rewards experimenting with movement.
Climbing and plant growth dominate the limited-length experience, so optional crystal hunts add more to do but not an entirely new core loop.
The soundtrack and ambient sound are perceived differently: one player remembers calm music fondly, while another hears relatively sparse musical accompaniment.
The story is a simple robotic mission backdrop for movement and environmental play rather than a complex character-driven narrative.
A Russian-language player describes the robot's electronic vocal noises as an occasional irritation despite broadly enjoying the experience.

conflicts.statement: The deliberate grip physics are part of the game's charm but can feel ungainly; playful audio similarly delights some and irritates others.
